pages.transcription:
24.XI.41
Dear Hanna, and Manfred,
We had no letter from you last week and hope
for one this week. Now it is already time, dearest Hanna, to send our
best wishes - I am sorry I cannot send anything else and wish you
would buy yourself something nice from us for your birthday and
hope that you spend the day pleasantly and in good spirits. Let us
wish that the next one Eva is already back at home! We had two letters
from her recently, both very cheerful, telling about all sorts of things.
Mrs. Schaeffer has been very unlucky, breaking her right arm several
times and for a little while her activity will be missing in the house.
But she is at home and up, and maybe this gives her more time for the
children. - Last week Eva was invited for the weekend at my sister-
in-laws, and she wrote me that she enjoyed Eva's visit. It seems to
have been a busy week-end for Eva, Stefanie took her to an ice-
show and a picture, then (she) had lunch with Mrs. Wiener apparently
at the old Morgenthan's house, for Stefanie wrote something about plates
of gold and silber, man servants etc and the Wiener's are not at all
like that. I am looking forward to Eva's report about the visit. My
sister-in-law seemed impressed by Eva's descriptions, I am more
interested to hear how she liked Mr and Mrs. Wiener, and hope that she
also enjoyed her time with the Zweigs. Also Salmon's seem to
have invited Eva recently and so I hope she had a good time.
Mrs. Sch. I am afraid will not be able to write for some time,
but I think you may be reassured about Eva. You miss Eva
and we miss Eva, and maybe we would even be a little hurt
if she did not miss us at all. But on the whole, I think she is
happy at Amity Hall. - Your birthday letter for Stefan travelled
very quickly and reached us some time ago. This week he will have
to pass this hard day and we plan to spend it with the
publisher in Friburgo, another little mountain town, 3 or 4 hours
from here. - Otherwise nothing is to be told about us. We had
a visitor or two, were invited once or twice, continue to play chess
(although Stefan is not satisfied with my progress), and the only new
thing is that I have begun to knit a jumper and taught my maid
how to make Semmelknoedel. Do not laugh at me if I ask you to
send me the recipe of Linzertorte and Lemon cream. I cannot give
"great" invitations but I feel the need to specialise as the things you
can buy here are always the same. Streuselkuchen or a kind of Petit
Four and I prefer home-made things, and whereas Sachertorte is rather
heavy and I believe impossible to make in my stove, I think Linzertorte
does not require much or regular heat. Do not think I develop into a
model housewife - even though I did go to the market last Saturday.
Yet I vaguely dream of making salt meat and would welcome a ladies
tea with stupid household talk. But I believe after December this
will be easy as many Brazilian friends send their families up here.
Fondest love and heartiest birthday wishes
Lotte.

[Randnotiz links:] I have been long without news from mother. And been wrote a few days ago that she was almost daily (and he seems to be recovering), so I hope that she is alright.
